title: OneNote on iPhone: Copilot chat pane with page summaries and Q&A
summary: The rollout, licensing requirement and licence-assignment instructions are supported. The governance section nevertheless contradicts itself: it calls licence assignment the only control tied to this feature, then documents a connected-experiences policy that also makes Copilot unavailable in OneNote on iOS.

claims.claim: Microsoft is introducing a Copilot chat pane in OneNote Mobile on iPhone.
claims.quote: Microsoft is introducing a new Copilot chat pane in OneNote Mobile (iPhone) for users licensed with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium).

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A price specific to this iPhone pane and Summary feature is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneNote" "Copilot" "iPhone" price credits meter licensing. Opened Microsoft Copilot overview and Meters for Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go services; read licensing search results. No feature-specific price found.

claims.claim: A meter or credit rate specific to this iPhone pane and Summary feature is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneNote" "Copilot" "iPhone" price credits meter licensing. Opened Microsoft Copilot overview and Meters for Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go services; the meters page describes agents, not a meter for this pane.

claims.claim: The licence assignment route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page.
2. Select a product.
3. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses containing SkuId, and an empty RemoveLicenses array assigns a licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyze content makes Copilot features unavailable in OneNote, rather than switching off just this pane.
claims.quote:
If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:
- Excel
- OneNote
- Outlook
- PowerPoint
- Word

claims.claim: The connected-experiences restriction applies to the most current OneNote app on iOS.
claims.quote: This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: The iOS privacy documentation names the Cloud Policy setting Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content.
claims.quote:
You can also use Cloud Policy and these four policy settings:
- Configure the level of client software diagnostic data sent by Office to Microsoft
- Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content

claims.claim: Cloud Policy configurations can be scoped to specific groups.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.where: Governance controls: first and second paragraphs
claims.claim: Licence assignment is the only control read and tied to this feature, despite the next paragraph documenting another applicable control.
claims.quote: The only control read and tied to this feature is licence assignment ... Turning off connected experiences that analyze content makes Copilot features unavailable in current OneNote apps on iOS
claims.fix: Remove the sentence 'The only control read and tied to this feature is licence assignment, because the notice says the pane depends on the Copilot (Premium) licence.' Keep the following paragraph explaining the broader connected-experiences control.
